source.title: Warhammer 40,000: The App 2.7.1, data build 972, released 2026-10-02

data.summary:
Each move type sets which units can make it, its **maximum distance** or **set-up distance**, and any conditions.

To move a unit:

- Move any of its models, each in turn, through as many straight-line moves and rotations as you like.
- Measure each straight line horizontally between matching points on the base at its start and end; the model’s running total for the move can’t exceed the move type’s maximum distance.
- Rotate a model any amount around its base centre, kept upright, at no distance cost; a model with no base turns on its central axis (Frame, 17.02).

Unless stated otherwise, a moving model:

- can pass through friendly models and any gap its base fits through
- can’t pass its base through enemy models or over the battlefield edge
- must meet every ‘While Moving’ condition

When you finish placing or moving models, check:

- the unit has coherency (03.03), if on the battlefield
- no model is on top of another model or part-embedded in a terrain feature’s surface, such as a wall or ceiling
- every ‘After Moving’ condition is met

If any check fails, the unit can’t make the move and its models go back to where they started; otherwise resolve the move type’s other ‘After Moving’ rules and the move ends.

Also:

- If the maximum distance uses M and the models’ M differ, each uses its own; with 1 model at 9" and the rest at 6", that model can go 9" and the others 6", with all other restrictions still applying.
- A model with a rule to move over or through models, or as if they weren’t there, can pass through enemy models but follows the move’s other restrictions.
- A move of up to X" has X" as its maximum distance.
- For random movement, see 02.02.03.
- Examples: 2 models each move 3" in one straight line and 3" in another, 6" in all; a model with a 12" maximum moves 6", rotates, moves 6" and rotates, 12" in all.
